assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1 receptor agonists is a rare chain from basic hormone biology to transformative therapy: glycaemic control, substantial weight loss and emerging cardiovascular, renal and possibly neurological benefit. Impact on patients and on the understanding of gut-brain-pancreas endocrinology is large and clear.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology, GLP-1/GLP-2 actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide) are the most defensible three. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is a strong industrial contributor but the credited set has four names for a three-person limit, and the Mojsov versus industry credit is contested; I flag that rather than treat it as settled.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy has been confirmed in many large independent trials over roughly two decades and the field is at peak clinical visibility, so recognition is timely. Long-term safety and non-metabolic benefits are still being defined, which does not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between Mojsov and others for the active peptide is disputed and my recollection of the details is not verified here.
Whether the prize should emphasise physiology or the drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of weight loss remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells expressing chimeric receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas, a new therapeutic modality with cell-therapy implications across oncology and now autoimmunity. Originality and clinical impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CD28-costimulated CAR design and preclinical proof), June (first clinical successes in CLL and ALL with 4-1BB CAR) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, TIL and early gene-engineered T cells) form a coherent set. Eshhar and others who conceived the original CAR are not in the credited names, which leaves a visible attribution gap I cannot resolve from this list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long follow-up for several indications confirm the concept, though activity in solid tumours is limited and toxicities (CRS, neurotoxicity, secondary malignancy signals) persist. Timely given maturity of the haematological data.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept lies partly outside the credited names.
Long-term safety signals continue to be evaluated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic dissection of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led directly to nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal infant disease into a treatable one. It validated antisense splicing modulation as a general therapeutic principle, a clear and clean example of mechanism-to-cure.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and development at Ionis) are both credited and together cover the decisive contributions. Adrian Krainer and Bennett share Lasker and Breakthrough-type recognition in my recollection but I have not verified this. Other contributors (Adrian Krainer's collaborators, the clinical trial leaders) are not credited, so the list may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up in thousands of patients; independent confirmation is strong and the therapeutic class has expanded. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Role of other groups in SMN2 biology and antisense chemistry may merit credit.
Real-world durability in adults and optimal timing of treatment still being clarified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and transformed experimental neuroscience, with spillover to cardiac and retinal applications, including early clinical restoration of vision. Originality and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The microbial rhodopsin channel characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenböck and others) are interleaved; six credited names cannot fit a three-person prize. Choosing Hegemann, Nagel and Deisseroth is a defensible compromise but arbitrarily omits Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, so attribution is the main obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over fifteen years; the technology is a standard tool. Clinical translation is nascent. Timing is appropriate for the tool, though some may view it as a methods prize rather than a discovery in physiology or medicine.
uncertainties: Six credited names make the three-laureate limit very contentious.
Whether a research tool fits the prize criteria for medicine as strongly as a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancers, and population data now show large reductions in cervical cancer incidence. Prevention of a major human cancer by vaccination is a landmark of importance and clear impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (co-development of the VLP approach, with Jian Zhou) form the usual core. Harald zur Hausen's earlier prize already addressed HPV causation, which clarifies the scope. Zhou's absence from the credited names is a gap, and I am unsure of the precise priority among VLP groups.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by national registry data across many countries with decade-plus follow-up; cervical cancer outcomes are now documented. Timely and arguably somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Priority among several VLP groups is disputed and not independently verified here.
Prior prize on HPV causation may lead to an argument that the area is already recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and its successors turned chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of targeted kinase inhibition against a defining oncogenic driver. Importance and clarity of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical and preclinical validation), Lydon (compound discovery programme) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a clean, widely recognised trio. Nowell, Hungerford, Rowley, Witte and others laid the BCR-ABL groundwork and are not credited, so the foundations of the discovery sit partly outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data and independent confirmation; the principle has been repeated across many cancers. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, which could count against it only in that earlier work may seem to have been the natural recipient.
uncertainties: Contributions of earlier BCR-ABL discoverers, some deceased, complicate fairness.
Chemistry credit within the company (e.g., Zimmermann) is not in the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and the demonstration that blockade works in rheumatoid arthritis opened biologic therapy for several autoimmune diseases, affecting millions of patients.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the established pair for the concept and clinical proof; a fair two-person configuration is supported. TNF cloning and engineered antibody work by others (e.g., Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias) fall outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by multiple agents and trials over twenty-five years, with biosimilars widely used. Maturity is not in doubt; it may be viewed as late and as a successor to recognition of immune checkpoint and other immunology prizes.
uncertainties: Priority and contributions of others in TNF biology are not credited.
Possible concern that the area has been partly covered by earlier immunology awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus or thalamus transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and is now a routine therapy with expansion to dystonia and other indications. As a clinician-neuroscientist I recognise the real-world benefit, though I treat this on the evidence rather than on any personal field affinity.
assessment.attribution: A single credited name, Benabid, is clear for the high-frequency stimulation discovery in Grenoble; however, DeLong's and Hallett's basal ganglia model and Benazzouz's, Limousin's and others' clinical work are not credited, so a one-person recognition may overstate his sole role.
assessment.maturity: Used for over three decades with robust randomised trial confirmation; mature and stable. Recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Sole credit leaves out the physiological basal ganglia model underpinning target selection.
The mechanism of action of DBS remains incompletely understood.
